paper_title: A Benchmark for Deep Information Synthesis
paper_content: This research paper introduces DEEPSYNTH, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents on complex real-world tasks that require synthesizing information from multiple sources. The benchmark aims to address the limitations of existing evaluations by focusing on realistic, time-consuming problems that demand information gathering, synthesis, and structured reasoning to derive insights beyond simple fact retrieval.

paper_title: LAMDA: A Longitudinal Android Malware Benchmark for Concept Drift Analysis

author_list.name: Md Ahsanul Haque
author_list.affiliation_name: University of Texas at El Paso

author_list.name: Ismail Hossain
author_list.affiliation_name: , University of Texas at El Paso

author_list.name: Md Mahmuduzzaman Kamol
author_list.affiliation_name: University of Texas at El Paso

author_list.name: Md Jahangir Alam
author_list.affiliation_name: University of Texas at El Paso

author_list.name: Sajedul Talukder
author_list.affiliation_name: , University of Texas at El Paso

author_list.name: Mohammad Saidur Rahman
author_list.affiliation_name: University of Texas at El Paso

paper_content: This paper introduces LAMDA, a comprehensive and temporally diverse benchmark dataset designed to analyze concept drift in Android malware detection. LAMDA addresses the limitations of existing datasets by providing over one million samples spanning 12 years, enabling in-depth research into the performance degradation of machine learning models over time due to the evolving nature of malware and the Android ecosystem.

paper_title: BrowseNet: Graph-Based Associative Memory for Contextual Information Retrieval
paper_content: This paper introduces BrowseNet, a novel framework for information retrieval from large document collections. BrowseNet leverages a graph-based associative memory approach to capture complex relationships between concepts, overcoming limitations of traditional retrieval methods. The system transforms text into a graph of interconnected document chunks, enabling efficient retrieval through query-specific subgraph exploration.

paper_title: Characterizing Deep Research: A Benchmark and Formal Definition
paper_content: This paper formally defines the "deep research" task, which involves complex search and reasoning beyond simple report generation. The authors introduce LIVEDRBENCH, a new benchmark with 100 challenging tasks, to objectively evaluate the performance of deep research systems by focusing on their ability to uncover intermediate claims.

paper_title: Social Agents: Collective Intelligence Improves LLM Predictions

author_list.name: Aanisha Bhattacharyya
author_list.affiliation_name: State University of New York at Buffalo
State University of New York at Buffalo

paper_content: This research introduces "Social Agents," a novel framework designed to enhance Large Language Model (LLM) predictions by simulating collective intelligence. The goal is to improve behavioral predictions by aggregating diverse, persona-based LLM outputs, mirroring the "Wisdom of Crowds" principle observed in human societies. This approach aims to outperform single-LLM predictions across various tasks, offering a more nuanced and accurate understanding of human responses.

paper_title: $\boldsymbol{\partial^\infty}$-Grid: A Neural Differential Equation Solver with Differentiable Feature Grids

author_list.name: Navami Kairanda
author_list.affiliation_name: Saarland Informatics Campus, Max Planck Institute for Informatics
Saarbruecken Research Center for Visual Computing, Interaction, and Artificial Intellligence
Saarland Informatics Campus, Max-Planck Institute for Informatics

paper_content: This paper introduces ∂[∞]-Grid, a novel neural network architecture designed for efficiently solving differential equations. It combines the speed of feature grids with infinitely differentiable radial basis function interpolation to overcome the limitations of existing methods, enabling faster and more accurate computation of derivatives. The research demonstrates a significant speed-up compared to coordinate-based MLPs across various physics-informed tasks.

paper_title: Efficient Approximate Posterior Sampling with Annealed Langevin Monte Carlo
paper_content: This research aims to efficiently sample from approximate posteriors in score-based generative models. The paper proposes a novel approach that allows for tractable sampling of a distribution closely matching the true posterior and a noised prior, achieving this in polynomial time.

paper_title: Ads that Stick: Near-Optimal Ad Optimization through Psychological Behavior Models

author_list.name: Kailash Gopal Darmasubramanian
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology, Madras, Dhirubhai Ambani Institute Of Information and Communication Technology

paper_content: This research aims to optimize ad scheduling by developing a model based on psychological principles like mere exposure, hedonic adaptation, and operant conditioning. The study introduces a near-optimal algorithm that determines the ideal timing and frequency of ad placements to maximize user interest, demonstrating its superiority over traditional heuristics.

paper_title: Pushing on Multilingual Reasoning Models with Language-Mixed Chain-of-Thought

author_list.name: Donghun Yang
author_list.affiliation_name: Korea Institute of Science and Technology  Information (KISTI)

author_list.name: Chanuk lim
author_list.affiliation_name: Korea Institute of Science and Technology Information (KISTI)

author_list.name: Kyong-Ha Lee
author_list.affiliation_name: Korea Institute of Science and Technology Information
Seoul National University, Seoul National University

paper_content: This research introduces Language-Mixed Chain-of-Thought (CoT), a novel reasoning schema that leverages English as an anchor while performing reasoning in a target language to enhance performance and minimize translation issues. The study presents a Korean case study, YI-SANG, and demonstrates that their proposed method significantly improves reasoning capabilities across various model sizes and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks.

paper_title: Cite Pretrain: Retrieval-Free Knowledge Attribution for Large Language Models
paper_content: This research investigates a novel method to enable large language models to reliably attribute their generated information to specific documents seen during pretraining, without requiring external retrieval at inference time. The goal is to improve the trustworthiness and verifiability of LLM outputs by revising the training process itself.

paper_title: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models via Intermediate Distribution Shaping
paper_content: This research paper aims to improve the fine-tuning of pre-trained diffusion models by shaping intermediate noise distributions. The authors introduce a novel method, P-GRAFT, and an algorithm called inverse noise correction, demonstrating their effectiveness in various generative tasks such as text-to-image and unconditional image generation.

paper_title: Fast Proteome-Scale Protein Interaction Retrieval via Residue-Level Factorization

author_list.name: Xinyu Yuan
author_list.affiliation_name: Montreal Institute for Learning Algorithms, University of Montreal, Université de Montréal

author_list.name: Qian Cong
author_list.affiliation_name: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

author_list.name: Jian Zhou
author_list.affiliation_name: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

paper_content: This paper introduces RaftPPI, a novel framework designed to efficiently predict protein-protein interactions (PPIs) at the proteome scale. The primary goal is to overcome the computational limitations of existing methods by developing a scalable approach that approximates residue-level interaction modeling for rapid retrieval of candidate interacting protein pairs.

paper_title: Tell me Habibi, is it Real or Fake?

author_list.name: Kartik Kuckreja
author_list.affiliation_name: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

author_list.name: Injy Hamed
author_list.affiliation_name: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

author_list.name: Muhammad Haris Khan
author_list.affiliation_name: Mohamed Bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

paper_content: This research aims to address the challenge of detecting deepfakes in multilingual and code-switched speech, particularly between Arabic and English. The paper introduces ArEnAV, a new large-scale audio-visual deepfake dataset designed to capture these linguistic complexities.

paper_title: The Art of Scaling Reinforcement Learning Compute for LLMs
paper_content: This research paper introduces a principled framework and the first large-scale study for analyzing and predicting the scaling of reinforcement learning (RL) compute in large language models (LLMs). The study aims to provide a scientific understanding and practical guidance for efficiently scaling RL training, moving it towards the predictability seen in LLM pre-training.

paper_title: Fathom-DeepResearch: Unlocking Long Horizon Information Retrieval and Synthesis for SLMs
paper_content: This research introduces Fathom-DeepResearch, a novel agentic system designed for complex, long-horizon information retrieval and synthesis. The system comprises two specialized models: Fathom-Search-4B, optimized for evidence-based web searching, and Fathom-Synthesizer-4B, which transforms search results into comprehensive reports.

paper_title: Exchangeability of GNN Representations  with Applications to Graph Retrieval
paper_content: This paper investigates the probabilistic symmetry, known as exchangeability, inherent in graph neural networks (GNNs). The research demonstrates that trained node embeddings from a broad range of GNNs are exchangeable random variables. This property allows for efficient graph similarity approximation using Euclidean distances on sorted embedding elements, leading to a unified framework for locality-sensitive hashing that improves graph retrieval effectiveness.

paper_title: Beyond Markovian Drifts: Action-Biased Geometric Walks with Memory for Personalized Summarization
paper_content: This research proposes Walk2Pers, a novel framework for personalized document summarization. It challenges the assumption of memoryless user preferences in existing models by introducing action-biased geometric walks with memory. Walk2Pers aims to better capture evolving user interests for more effective summarization.

paper_title: Factuality Matters: When Image Generation and Editing Meet Structured Visuals

author_list.name: Xi Chen
author_list.affiliation_name: the University of Hong Kong, University of Hong Kong
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

paper_content: This research addresses the challenge of generating and editing structured visuals like charts and diagrams, which current models struggle with due to requirements for composition planning, text rendering, and factual accuracy. The paper introduces a new dataset, a unified model, and a benchmark (StructBench) to advance capabilities in this domain, aiming to improve multimodal foundations for structured visual content.

paper_title: Non-Clashing Teaching in Graphs: Algorithms, Complexity, and Bounds

author_list.name: Sujoy Bhore
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay

paper_content: This paper investigates (positive) non-clashing teaching for closed neighborhoods in graphs, a fundamental concept in machine teaching. The research aims to improve upon existing algorithmic results by providing FPT algorithms for broader parameter classes, deriving stronger lower bounds, and establishing combinatorial upper bounds for more extensive graph categories.

paper_title: TSPulse: Tiny Pre-Trained Models with Disentangled Representations for Rapid Time-Series Analysis
paper_content: This paper introduces TSPulse, a family of ultra-light pre-trained models designed for rapid time-series analysis. The goal is to address the limitations of existing models by disentangling heterogeneous signals into specialized embedding views, enabling effective zero-shot transfer for diagnostic tasks. TSPulse achieves state-of-the-art performance on various tasks with significantly smaller model sizes, promoting efficient deployment.

paper_title: Regulating Internal Alignment Flows for Robust Learning Under Spurious Correlations

author_list.name: Rajeev Ranjan Dwivedi
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Bhopal

author_list.name: Mohammedkaif Mohammedrafiq Kalagond
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research

author_list.name: Niramay M.Patel
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research

paper_content: This research paper introduces Alignment-Gated Suppression (AGS), a novel plug-in regularizer designed to improve the robustness of deep learning models. AGS intervenes internally during training to suppress spurious correlations, thereby enhancing worst-group accuracy without requiring group labels.

paper_title: Executable Counterfactuals: Improving LLMs' Causal Reasoning Through Code
paper_content: This research introduces "Executable Counterfactuals," a novel framework designed to accurately assess and enhance Large Language Models' (LLMs) causal reasoning capabilities. The framework operationalizes counterfactual reasoning through code and math problems, ensuring all three essential steps—abduction, intervention, and prediction—are explicitly addressed. This approach facilitates the creation of scalable synthetic data for rigorous evaluation, revealing significant performance gaps in current LLMs and demonstrating the efficacy of reinforcement learning for improvement.

paper_title: IndicVisionBench: Benchmarking Cultural and Multilingual Understanding in VLMs

author_list.name: Akash
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Information Technology Allahabad

paper_content: This paper introduces IndicVisionBench, a large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate vision-language models (VLMs) in culturally diverse and multilingual settings, specifically focusing on the Indian subcontinent. The benchmark aims to address the limitations of existing Western-centric evaluations by providing a resource for assessing VLM performance across 10 Indian languages and English in tasks like OCR, MMT, and VQA.

paper_title: SmartChunk Retrieval: Query-Aware Chunk Compression with Planning for Efficient Document RAG
paper_content: This paper introduces SmartChunk Retrieval, a novel framework designed to improve the efficiency and accuracy of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for long documents. The system employs a query-aware planner to determine optimal chunk abstraction levels and a compression module for high-level embeddings, thus adapting retrieval granularity dynamically to balance performance and cost.

paper_title: Constructive Distortion: Improving MLLMs with Attention-Guided Image Warping

author_list.name: Hyeonjeong Ha
author_list.affiliation_name: Department of Computer Science, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

paper_content: This paper introduces AttWarp, a novel method designed to improve the performance of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). AttWarp addresses MLLMs' tendency to miss small details and spatial relationships in cluttered scenes by dynamically reallocating image resolution towards task-relevant regions. The method uses cross-modal attention to guide this warping process, enhancing fine-grained perception and reasoning without altering the MLLM's architecture or weights.

paper_title: f-INE: A Hypothesis Testing Framework for Estimating Influence under Training Randomness

author_list.name: Prathosh AP
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Science, Indian institute of science, Bangalore

paper_content: This paper introduces f-INE, a novel hypothesis testing framework for estimating the influence of individual data points on machine learning models. Its primary goal is to overcome the instability of existing methods, which often collapse under training randomness, by explicitly accounting for this variability. The f-INE framework enables reliable influence estimation, facilitating tasks like data curation and debugging.

paper_title: Automated Stateful Specialization for Adaptive Agent Systems

author_list.name: Harrish Ayyanar
author_list.affiliation_name: University College London, University of London

paper_content: This research paper introduces ASPEC, a novel framework designed to automate the creation and adaptation of agent systems. ASPEC addresses the limitations of existing approaches by enabling the development of stateful teams of specialist agents that accumulate knowledge over time and can be reconfigured for new tasks without human intervention. The goal is to create agent systems that are simultaneously expert, adaptive, and efficient.

paper_title: Welfarist Formulations for Diverse Similarity Search

author_list.name: Nirjhar Das
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Science, Indian institute of science, Bangalore

paper_content: This paper introduces novel welfare-based formulations for Nearest Neighbor Search (NNS) that prioritize both relevance and diversity among search results. It proposes a flexible, query-dependent approach that adaptively balances these two objectives, unlike previous methods that imposed fixed diversity constraints. The research also presents efficient algorithms with provable guarantees to achieve these objectives.

paper_title: Graph-Theoretic Intrinsic Reward: Guiding RL with Effective Resistance

author_list.name: Jatin Chauhan
author_list.affiliation_name: Fujitsu Research and Development Center Co. Ltm.

author_list.name: Shivam Bhardwaj
author_list.affiliation_name: Fujitsu Research and Development Center Co. Ltm.

author_list.name: Aditya Saibewar
author_list.affiliation_name: Fujitsu Research and Development Center Co. Ltm.

author_list.name: Aditya Ramesh
author_list.affiliation_name: Fujitsu Research and Development Center Co. Ltm.

author_list.name: Sadbhavana Babar
author_list.affiliation_name: Fujitsu Research and Development Center Co. Ltm.
Fujitsu Research and Development Center Co. Ltm.

paper_content: This paper introduces a novel graph-theoretic intrinsic reward signal called "Effective Resistance" to guide reinforcement learning agents in dynamic environments with sparse rewards. The proposed method aims to improve exploration efficiency and policy robustness by directly correlating the reward signal with successful goal-reaching states. Theoretical guarantees and extensive empirical analysis demonstrate significant performance improvements over state-of-the-art baselines.

paper_title: GeoDiv: Framework for Measuring Geographical Diversity in Text-to-Image Models

author_list.name: Mohana Singh
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Science, Indian institute of science, Bangalore

paper_content: This research introduces GeoDiv, a novel framework designed to measure geographical diversity in text-to-image models. GeoDiv aims to overcome the limitations of existing metrics by assessing economic and visual variations, revealing biases in how different regions are depicted. The framework's application demonstrates a consistent lack of geographical diversity and highlights socio-economic stereotypes in generated images.

paper_title: Hyperbolic Aware Minimization: Implicit Bias for Sparsity

author_list.name: Tom Jacobs
author_list.affiliation_name: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security

author_list.name: Celia Rubio-Madrigal
author_list.affiliation_name: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security

author_list.name: Rebekka Burkholz
author_list.affiliation_name: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security

paper_content: This paper introduces Hyperbolic Aware Minimization (HAM), a novel optimization technique designed to enhance the generalization capabilities of deep learning models, particularly for sparse training. HAM achieves this by alternating standard optimization steps with a computationally efficient hyperbolic mirror step, which mitigates a key bottleneck in parameter movement and effectively promotes sparsity.

paper_title: CIMemories: A Compositional Benchmark For Contextual Integrity In LLMs
paper_content: This research introduces CIMemories, a new benchmark designed to evaluate how well Large Language Models (LLMs) control information flow from their memory based on task context. The benchmark uses synthetic user profiles with diverse attributes and various task scenarios to identify inappropriate information leakage, highlighting limitations in current frontier models.

paper_title: Zero-shot Forecasting by Simulation Alone
paper_content: This research introduces SarSim0, a novel time-series simulation pipeline designed to address challenges in zero-shot forecasting. The primary goal is to generate synthetic time-series data rapidly and effectively, enabling strong zero-shot forecasting performance on complex benchmarks. By training models on these simulations, the research demonstrates significant improvements over existing methods, even surpassing the generative models themselves.

paper_title: Why DPO is a Misspecified Estimator and How to Fix It
paper_content: This paper identifies that Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) can be a misspecified estimator when the true reward function is not achievable by the parametric policy class. This misspecification leads to undesirable outcomes such as preference order reversal and worsened policy rewards. To address this, the authors propose AuxDPO, an extension of DPO that incorporates auxiliary variables to guide the optimization towards the intended solution and mitigate DPO's limitations.

paper_title: A Dense Subset Index for Collective Query Coverage

author_list.name: Pritish Chakraborty
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay

paper_content: This research aims to develop a novel indexing technique for dense retrieval systems. The goal is to efficiently retrieve small collections of corpus items whose information collectively covers the query's intent, moving beyond traditional single-item relevance scoring.

paper_title: Enhancing Trustworthiness of Fine-Tuned LLMs via Regularized Subset Selection

author_list.name: Kumar Shubham
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Science, Indian institute of science, Bangalore

author_list.name: Nishant Sharma
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Science, Indian institute of science, Bangalore

author_list.name: Karn Tiwari
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Science, Indian institute of science, Bangalore

author_list.name: Prathosh AP
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Science, Indian institute of science, Bangalore

paper_content: This paper aims to enhance the trustworthiness of large language models (LLMs) after supervised fine-tuning without extensive retraining. The proposed method identifies and selectively retrains the model on problematic training samples using a computationally efficient two-stage process. This approach significantly improves trustworthiness metrics while preserving downstream performance.

paper_title: Text2Arch: A Dataset for Generating Scientific Architecture Diagrams from Natural Language Descriptions
paper_content: This paper introduces TEXT2ARCH, a new dataset designed to facilitate the automatic generation of scientific architecture diagrams from natural language descriptions. The goal is to bridge the gap between textual representations and visual diagrams, enabling applications in software engineering, documentation, and education.

paper_title: GAVEL: Towards Rule-Based Safety through Activation Monitoring

author_list.name: Shir Rozenfeld
author_list.affiliation_name: Ben Gurion University of the Negev

author_list.name: Itay Zloczower
author_list.affiliation_name: Ben Gurion University of the Negev

author_list.name: Eyal Lenga
author_list.affiliation_name: Ben Gurion University of the Negev

paper_content: This paper introduces GAVEL, a novel framework for rule-based safety in large language models (LLMs) that utilizes activation monitoring. GAVEL models internal model activations as interpretable "cognitive elements" and defines predicate rules over these elements to detect nuanced, domain-specific harmful behaviors with higher precision and flexibility than existing methods. This approach aims to enhance AI governance by providing transparent, auditable, and easily configurable safety mechanisms without requiring model retraining.

paper_title: Scalable Random Wavelet Features: Efficient Non-Stationary Kernel Approximation with Convergence Guarantees
paper_content: This paper introduces Random Wavelet Features (RWF), a novel framework designed to efficiently approximate non-stationary kernels. RWF leverages the properties of wavelets to create scalable kernel methods that can capture input-dependent patterns, overcoming the limitations of stationary approximations. The research demonstrates RWF's superior performance and accuracy-efficiency trade-off compared to existing methods for complex, non-stationary problems.

paper_title: Is Graph Unlearning Ready for Practice? A Benchmark on Efficiency, Utility, and Forgetting
paper_content: This paper introduces the first comprehensive benchmark for Graph Unlearning, evaluating existing methods on efficiency, utility, and forgetting capabilities. The research aims to determine if these unlearning techniques are practical alternatives to retraining for Graph Neural Networks, especially in sensitive applications. Findings indicate that most current methods are not yet suitable for large-scale graphs, but the study provides guidelines for selecting appropriate techniques and identifies future research directions.

paper_title: FlowCast: Trajectory Forecasting for Scalable Zero-Cost Speculative Flow Matching

author_list.name: Divya Jyoti Bajpai
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay, Dhirubhai Ambani Institute Of Information and Communication Technology

paper_content: This research introduces FlowCast, a novel framework designed to accelerate inference for Flow Matching (FM) generative models without compromising output quality. The primary goal is to enable real-time and interactive applications by efficiently skipping redundant denoising steps through speculative trajectory forecasting based on constant velocity assumptions.

paper_title: Certified Evaluation of Model-Level Explanations for Graph Neural Networks
paper_content: This research paper introduces a novel framework for evaluating model-level explanations of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). The goal is to move beyond simple class scores to formally assess the sufficiency and quality of explanations by quantifying their ability to represent the GNN's reasoning. The paper proposes theoretically grounded metrics that provide statistically reliable comparisons between different GNN explanation methods.

paper_title: On Discovering Algorithms for Adversarial Imitation Learning
paper_content: This paper investigates the discovery of data-driven reward assignment functions for Adversarial Imitation Learning (AIL). The researchers propose Discovered Adversarial Imitation Learning (DAIL), a meta-learnt AIL algorithm that utilizes an LLM-guided evolutionary framework to discover these functions. DAIL demonstrates improved stability and generalizes across different environments and policy optimization algorithms, outperforming existing human-designed methods.

paper_title: THE PATH OF LEAST RESISTANCE: GUIDING LLM REASONING TRAJECTORIES WITH PREFIX CONSENSUS
paper_content: This paper introduces "Path of Least Resistance" (PoLR), a novel inference-time method for Large Language Models (LLMs) designed to improve reasoning efficiency. PoLR leverages prefix consensus to significantly reduce computational costs and latency by clustering short reasoning prefixes and focusing expansion on the most dominant cluster. This approach maintains the accuracy of computationally expensive methods like Self-Consistency while offering substantial performance gains.

paper_title: KLAS: Using Similarity to Stitch Neural Networks for Improved Accuracy-Efficiency Tradeoffs
paper_content: This research introduces KLAS, a novel framework designed to improve the accuracy-efficiency trade-offs of neural networks. KLAS achieves this by intelligently selecting how to "stitch" together pretrained models, leveraging KL divergence to better capture model similarities. The goal is to create a wider range of deployment options with superior performance compared to existing methods.

paper_title: Poisson Midpoint Method for Log Concave Sampling: Beyond the Strong Error Lower Bounds
paper_content: This paper analyzes the Poisson Midpoint Method for sampling from strongly log-concave distributions using Langevin dynamics. The goal is to achieve a cubic speedup in convergence rate compared to standard Euler-Maruyama discretization, surpassing existing bounds for randomized midpoint methods. The research also demonstrates that for underdamped Langevin dynamics, the convergence complexity in 2-Wasserstein distance can be significantly better than established lower bounds for strong L2 error.

paper_title: Universal Model Routing for Efficient LLM Inference
paper_content: This paper introduces UniRoute, a novel approach for efficient Large Language Model (LLM) inference. UniRoute enables dynamic routing to new, unseen LLMs at test time by representing each LLM as a feature vector derived from predictions on representative prompts. The proposed method offers theoretically grounded routing rules and demonstrates effectiveness in experiments with numerous unseen LLMs.

paper_title: Contraction and Hourglass Persistence for Learning on Graphs, Simplices, and Cells

author_list.name: Mattie Ji
author_list.affiliation_name: University of Pennsylvania, University of Pennsylvania

paper_content: This paper aims to improve Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) by addressing limitations in current methods that use topological features. The research introduces "Contraction Homology" and "Hourglass Persistence" as novel topological descriptors designed to enhance the expressivity and learnability of GNNs, with practical applications demonstrated on real-world graph datasets.

paper_title: Riemannian Federated Learning via Averaging Gradient Streams
paper_content: This paper introduces RFedAGS, a novel Riemannian Federated Learning algorithm designed to address challenges like partial agent participation and data heterogeneity. The algorithm achieves global convergence and sublinear convergence rates, with performance validated through extensive experiments.

paper_title: Robust Reward Modeling via Causal Rubrics
paper_content: This paper introduces CROME, a novel framework designed to mitigate reward hacking in large language models by explicitly modeling causal relationships. CROME employs a causally robust reward modeling strategy that utilizes targeted synthetic augmentations to distinguish genuine quality drivers from spurious correlations, leading to more aligned and reliable LLM policies.

paper_title: Data-Aware and Scalable Sensitivity Analysis for Decision Tree Ensembles

author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay

paper_content: This paper introduces a novel data-aware framework for analyzing the sensitivity of decision tree ensembles to specific features. The primary goal is to generate realistic and interpretable examples of how model predictions can be altered by manipulating certain input features, thereby enhancing the trustworthiness of these models in critical applications. The framework achieves this by ensuring sensitive examples remain close to the training data distribution, utilizing advanced techniques like MILP and SMT encodings for scalability and efficiency.

paper_title: CERTIFIED VS. EMPIRICAL ADVERSARIAL ROBUSTNESS VIA HYBRID CONVOLUTIONS WITH ATTENTION STOCHASTICITY
paper_content: This research introduces HyCAS, a novel adversarial defense mechanism. The primary goal of HyCAS is to significantly reduce the discrepancy between theoretical (certified) and practical (empirical) robustness against adversarial attacks. It achieves this by integrating deterministic and randomized components within a neural network architecture.

paper_title: FrugalRAG: Less is More in RL Finetuning for Multi-hop Question Answering
paper_content: This paper introduces FrugalRAG, a novel framework for efficiently fine-tuning retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models for multi-hop question answering. The goal is to optimize both accuracy and efficiency by adaptively reducing retrieval steps based on question difficulty, achieving state-of-the-art performance with significantly less training data.

paper_title: Testing Fourier Sparsity via Implicit Sensing
paper_content: This paper aims to test the Fourier sparsity of a Boolean function, determining if it is significantly sparse or far from any sparse function. The research presents a novel algorithm with improved query complexity and establishes a new lower bound on the number of queries required for this task.

paper_title: Sculpting Subspaces: Constrained Full Fine-Tuning in LLMs for Continual Learning

author_list.affiliation_name: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

author_list.name: Hao Wang
author_list.affiliation_name: RedHat AI & MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab

paper_content: This research introduces Orthogonal Subspace Fine-Tuning (OSFT), a novel parameter-efficient method for continual learning in large language models (LLMs). OSFT aims to prevent catastrophic forgetting by preserving critical parameter subspaces from prior knowledge and constraining new task updates to be orthogonal to these subspaces. This approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in balancing task learnability and knowledge retention without increasing parameter count or requiring task-specific gradients.

paper_title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation

author_list.name: Zachary S Siegel
author_list.affiliation_name: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Electrical Engineering & Computer Science

author_list.name: Dongyoon Hahm
author_list.affiliation_name: Korea Advanced Institute of Science & Technology

author_list.name: Juyong Lee
author_list.affiliation_name: Korea Advanced Institute of Science & Technology

paper_content: This paper introduces the Holistic Agent Leaderboard (HAL), a standardized evaluation framework designed to address the significant challenges in assessing AI agent performance. HAL aims to provide a more reliable and comprehensive understanding of agent capabilities by improving evaluation speed, cost control, and the detection of exploitative or erroneous behaviors. The authors' ultimate goal is to shift the focus from agents that merely excel on benchmarks to those that demonstrate reliable real-world performance.

paper_title: FastFlow: Accelerating The Generative Flow Matching Models with Bandit Inference

author_list.name: Divya Jyoti Bajpai
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay, Dhirubhai Ambani Institute Of Information and Communication Technology

author_list.name: Aashay Sandansing
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay, Dhirubhai Ambani Institute Of Information and Communication Technology

paper_content: This paper introduces FastFlow, an adaptive inference framework designed to accelerate generative flow matching models. FastFlow efficiently skips unnecessary denoising steps by approximating them using finite-difference velocity estimates. This approach optimizes the trade-off between speed and generation quality through a multi-armed bandit strategy, achieving significant speedups without requiring retraining or compromising output fidelity.

paper_title: Efficient algorithms for Incremental Metric Bipartite Matching

author_list.name: Ritesh Seth
author_list.affiliation_name: Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology, Delhi

author_list.name: Mrinal Garg
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay

author_list.name: Sujoy Bhore
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay

author_list.name: Syamantak Das
author_list.affiliation_name: Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology, Delhi

paper_content: This paper introduces an efficient, deterministic algorithm for incremental minimum-cost bipartite matching in arbitrary metric spaces. The goal is to maintain an approximate minimum-cost matching with an amortized insertion time, addressing the computational challenges of dynamic settings where new points arrive over time. The algorithm is designed to be significantly faster than recomputing matches from scratch and is amenable to parallelization on both CPUs and GPUs.

paper_title: A Noise is Worth Diffusion Guidance

author_list.name: Jiwon Kang

paper_content: This paper introduces NoiseRefine, a novel framework designed to enhance the quality of images generated by diffusion models. NoiseRefine achieves this by training a network to refine the initial Gaussian noise into a "guidance-distilled" noise space. This approach aims to improve image fidelity without the computational cost typically associated with guidance methods.

paper_title: In Agents We Trust, but Who Do Agents Trust? Latent Source Preferences Steer LLM Generations

author_list.name: Krishna P. Gummadi
author_list.affiliation_name: Max Planck Institute for Software Systems

paper_content: This research investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs), when acting as agents, exhibit inherent preferences for information originating from certain sources. The study aims to uncover these latent source preferences and understand how they influence the information presented to users.

paper_content: The paper introduces KALEIDOSCOPE, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) across multiple languages and cultures. Its goal is to address the limitations of English-centric evaluations by providing an in-language, large-scale, and culturally authentic assessment framework.

paper_title: vCache: Verified Semantic Prompt Caching

author_list.name: Aditya Desai
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay

paper_content: This paper introduces vCache, a novel verified semantic caching system designed to address the limitations of traditional semantic caches. vCache aims to provide predictable performance by guaranteeing user-defined error rates, which static thresholding methods currently fail to do. Through an online learning approach, vCache dynamically optimizes caching thresholds, leading to significant improvements in cache hit rates and error reduction compared to existing systems.

paper_title: MIRACLE: Model-free Imitation and Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Cut-Selection

author_list.name: Rijul Tandon
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology, Madras, Dhirubhai Ambani Institute Of Information and Communication Technology

paper_content: This research introduces MIRACLE, a novel framework for adaptive cut-selection in Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) solvers. The primary goal is to significantly reduce memory consumption and improve solving efficiency by intelligently selecting cutting planes, rather than generating a large number of them. MIRACLE achieves this by employing imitation learning and reinforcement learning to mimic expert solver decisions and dynamically adjust computational resources.

paper_title: TaTToo: Tool-Grounded Thinking PRM for Test-Time Scaling in Tabular Reasoning

author_list.name: Jiaru Zou
author_list.affiliation_name: Department of Computer Science, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

paper_content: This paper addresses the lack of reliable step-level supervision for Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) performing tabular reasoning. The authors introduce TATTOO, a novel Process Reward Model (PRM) designed to provide precise supervision for table-specific reasoning steps by integrating tool capabilities and grounding rewards in table content.

paper_title: Towards Cognitively-Faithful Decision-Making Models to Improve AI Alignment
paper_content: This paper aims to develop AI models that better reflect human cognitive decision-making processes. By using an axiomatic approach that considers how humans process information, the research seeks to create more accurate and interpretable models for AI alignment, especially in high-stakes situations.

paper_title: Algorithmic Guarantees for Distilling Supervised and Offline RL Datasets
paper_content: This paper introduces an efficient algorithm for dataset distillation, a process that creates a smaller synthetic dataset for model training. The algorithm achieves algorithmic guarantees for both supervised learning (regression) and offline reinforcement learning (RL), ensuring that models trained on the synthetic data perform comparably to those trained on the original, larger dataset. The work provides theoretical bounds on the number of sampled regressors needed and demonstrates practical performance gains through extensive experiments.

paper_title: vAttention: Verified Sparse Attention via Sampling

author_list.name: Aditya Desai
author_list.affiliation_name: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay

paper_content: This paper introduces vAttention, a novel sparse attention mechanism designed to address the limitations of existing methods in approximating full attention for large language models. Unlike prior approaches lacking guarantees on approximation quality, vAttention provides user-specified accuracy guarantees (ϵ, δ) and unifies top-k and sampling strategies. This leads to significant improvements in sparse attention quality, effectively bridging the gap between full and sparse attention and enabling faster decoding without compromising model performance.
